questions.question: An/A ______ is a finite set of instructions which, when followed, accomplish a particular task.

• An **algorithm**__ is a finite set of instructions that, if followed, accomplishes a particular task.
 
• It is the step by step procedure for solving any problem.
 
• Algorithms are used to specify how calculations, data processing, automated reasoning, automated decision-making, and other tasks should be carried out.
 
• All algorithms must meet the following requirements:
 
 
• The **inputs** to an algorithm can be zero or more and come from a specific set of objects.
 
• An algorithm has one or more **outputs** that are related to the inputs in some way.

• After a **finite number of steps**, the algorithm must always end.

questions.question: ______ is an interpreted, high-level and general-purpose programming language.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Python**__.

__
 
• **Python is an interpreted, object-oriented, high-level programming language with dynamic semantics**__.

 __
 
• Its high-level data structure, coupled with dynamic typing and dynamic binding, make it very attractive for rapid application development as well as for use as a scripting or glue language for linking existing components together.
 
• Python's simple, easy-to-learn syntax emphasizes readability and therefore reduces program maintenance costs.
 
• Python supports modules and packages, which encourage program modularity and code reuse.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Different Types of Computer Language**

 
 
• **Machine Language**

 
 
• The machine language is sometimes referred to as machine code or object code which is set of binary digits 0 and 1. These binary digits are understood and read by a computer system and interpret easily.
 
• It is considered a native language as it can be directly understood by a central processing unit (CPU).
 
 
 
• **Assembly Language**
 
 
• The assembly language is considered a low-level language for microprocessors and many other programmable devices.
 
• The assembly language is also considered a second-generation language.
 
• The first generation language is machine language.
 
 
 
• **High-Level Language**
 
 
• The development of high-level language was done when the programmers face the issue in writing programs as the older language has portability issues which means the code written in one machine cannot be transferred to other machines.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of network that allows users from outside to access the Intranet of an organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extranet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **Extranet** is a private network that leverages internet technology and the public telecommunication system to securely share part of a business's information or operations with suppliers, vendors, partners, customers, or other businesses.
 
• It allows controlled access to the organization's internal information from outside the organization's intranet.
 
• Extranets improve efficiency by providing a secure environment to exchange data, manage projects, and collaborate with external stakeholders.
 
• Security measures such as encryption, user authentication, and firewalls are typically employed to ensure that the data shared over an Extranet remains secure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• An Intranet is a private network accessible only to an organization's staff.
 
• It is used to share company information and computing resources among employees.
 
• Intranets improve communication, collaboration, and efficiency within an organization.
 
 
 
• **Internet:**
 
 
• The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate freely and share information worldwide.
 
• It is publicly accessible and used for a variety of purposes, including communication, research, and commerce.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Private Network (VPN):**
 
 
• A VPN creates a secure, encrypted connection over a less secure network, such as the internet.
 
• It enables users to send and receive data as if their devices were directly connected to the private network.
 
 
 
• **Firewall:**
 
 
• A firewall is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's previously established security policies.
 
• It acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks, such as the internet.

questions.question: What does ‘CC’ stand for in the context of email?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon Copy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'CC' in email stands for **Carbon Copy**.
 
• It is used to send a copy of the email to recipients other than the primary recipient.
 
• Recipients listed in the CC field can see who else has received the email.
 
• It is typically used to keep individuals informed without requiring them to take any action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BCC (Blind Carbon Copy)**:

 
 
• This field is used to send a copy of the email to recipients without disclosing their email addresses to the other recipients.
 
• It is useful for maintaining the privacy of email addresses.
 
 
 
• **Email Etiquette**:
 
 
• Use CC sparingly to avoid overwhelming recipients with unnecessary emails.
 
• Ensure that the primary recipient is aware of who is included in the CC field.
 
 
 
• **History of CC**:
 
 
• The term originates from the practice of using carbon paper to create copies of documents.
 
• In email, it serves a similar function of making copies of the message for additional recipients.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between To, CC, and BCC**:
 
 
• **To**: The primary recipient(s) of the email.
 
• **CC**: Secondary recipients who are visible to all other recipients.
 
• **BCC**: Secondary recipients who are not visible to other recipients.
